title: gen7_net: faster suit-net forward pass (~2.7x; rollouts ~2.4x), same outputs
head: 8a45f23ea35fa335fcccf94cb70ad920b77825a7
body:
**Problem.** For Stu-style pure rollouts, the policy/rollout net's forward pass is ~92% of rollout time (cProfile, see below). The suit net ran four of its layers as numpy matmuls on 3-D arrays, which numpy executes as one small product per row. It also computed the trunk's share of the decoder's first layer four times per row, once per suit.

**Change** (`bridge_harness/gen7_net.py`, kind 1 only):
- `dense()` flattens to one 2-D product for `ws0`, `ws1`, `wd0` and `wd1`.
- `wd0` is split by input part: [suit encoding | trunk | slot]. The trunk part is computed once per row and broadcast.

Outputs are identical up to float rounding (max |diff| ~1e-6). Play is unchanged, so this needs no new bot identity. But it is a runtime change: frozen runs only pick it up if their owner moves them to it.

**Measured** in a 2-core Xeon sandbox, single-threaded (`OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1`). Net: 768-wide suit net. Rollout net v2 (`runs/w768/policy.npz` on `transfer/rollout-net-v2-20261113`, sha256 `8f87aa8f52ae2c11…`) has exactly these shapes. Positions: test-fixture deals at trick 7 (24 random plies), 128 layouts × 4 cards, `Seats([net], mode='draw')`, no claim finder.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| forward pass, 512-row batch | 7.6k rows/s | 20.6k rows/s (2.7×) |
| whole `x8_rollout.evaluate`, 6 decisions | 7.5k rows/s | 17.3k rows/s (2.3×) |
| `evaluate`, 32 layouts | 6.5k rows/s | 16.1k rows/s (2.5×) |

The before and after runs made the same number of net rows (55,744), i.e. the same play. Stu's Azure logs (`transfer/rollout-loop-azure3-20261113`, runs l0/g0/pf) show ~5.8k rows/s inside x8, which suggests the same bottleneck. The speedup on the AMD (Zen 4) cores has not been measured.

**Tests.**
- New: `tests/test_gen7_net_forward.py` compares every head against the plain layer-by-layer form.
- `tests/test_gen7.py` and `tests/test_gen7_alpha.py` pass on this branch (44 tests).
- On `research/rollout-loop-20261113`, the same edit plus `test_x8`, `test_rollout_net` and `test_plan_rollout`: 73 passed, 7 skipped (need `SURE_BIN`).
- The JAX training path was not run; the change uses only reshape, slicing and matmul.

**Applying to Stu's branch.** This commit cherry-picks cleanly onto `research/rollout-loop-20261113`. The SiD-student head (`wd1s`) exists only there and stays a 3-D matmul. That is correct but not sped up; use `dense(d, params['wd1s'])` there for the same gain.

**Follow-ups measured, not included.** Real v2 weights, 37,951 rollout rows, decoder/output layers via ONNX Runtime, single-threaded:

| | dense part vs ORT fp32 | top-card changes vs fp32 | mean total-variation distance |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 (rounding emulated, fp32 accumulate) | not timed (needs oneDNN or PyTorch) | 0.16% | 0.0016 |
| int8 dynamic, per-channel weights, AMX blocked | 2.4× | 2.6% | 0.021 |
| int8 dynamic, per-tensor | 2.5× | 13.7% | 0.116 |

ORT fp32 alone is about 1.2× faster than numpy on the dense part. The accuracy figures use fixture positions with a random hand-fit scorer feeding `shown`, so they are indicative; arena positions are the real test.
